reading: Each coloured cell becomes a full square ring centred on the grid centre, at radius equal to its Chebyshev distance from the centre; the rings fill the whole grid.

slots.rings: one per non-background cell; radius = max(|dy|,|dx|) from the centre; colour = that cell's colour
slots.rest: every cell is covered by exactly one ring (the background disappears)

why: every radius 0..R has exactly one coloured cell, so each output cell takes the colour of the cell whose radius equals its own

reading: Closed-loop objects (with a hole) slide straight up and crosses/open shapes slide straight down; each group stacks like gravity, ignoring the other group.

slots.motion: each object moves vertically until it hits the grid edge or an already-settled object of the same group; nearest-to-edge objects settle first

why: every object keeps shape and column; hollow ones end at the top, the others at the bottom

reading: Red cells with no orthogonal red neighbour turn blue (1); all other cells stay.

new_rows.name: lone4
new_rows.datalog:
tw(Y, X, C) :- px(Y, X, C), C > 0.
nb(Y, X) :- tw(Y, X, C), Y2 = Y + 1, tw(Y2, X, C).
nb(Y, X) :- tw(Y, X, C), Y2 = Y - 1, tw(Y2, X, C).
nb(Y, X) :- tw(Y, X, C), X2 = X + 1, tw(Y, X2, C).
nb(Y, X) :- tw(Y, X, C), X2 = X - 1, tw(Y, X2, C).
lone4(Y, X) :- tw(Y, X, C), !nb(Y, X).

why: exactly the non-zero cells without a 4-neighbour of their colour change, 2 -> 1 (diagonal contact does not count; in two pairs 2 is the most common colour, so the row uses px, not cell)

reading: Among several 8-framed squares with red patterns inside (noise 8 pixels around), output the one square whose red pattern is unique.

new_rows.name: odd_square
new_rows.datalog:
two(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 2.
near(Y, X, Y2, X2) :- two(Y, X), two(Y2, X2), DY = Y2 - Y, DX = X2 - X, DY >= -2, DY <= 2, DX >= -2, DX <= 2.
reach(Y, X, Y2, X2) :- near(Y, X, Y2, X2).
reach(Y, X, Y3, X3) :- reach(Y, X, Y2, X2), near(Y2, X2, Y3, X3).
cid(Y, X, min(K)) :- reach(Y, X, Y2, X2), K = Y2 * 100 + X2.
ky(K, min(Y)) :- cid(Y, X, K).
kx(K, min(X)) :- cid(Y, X, K).
rel(K, DY, DX) :- cid(Y, X, K), ky(K, Y0), kx(K, X0), DY = Y - Y0, DX = X - X0.
differ(K1, K2) :- rel(K1, DY, DX), ky(K2, A), !rel(K2, DY, DX).
twin(K1) :- ky(K1, A), ky(K2, B), K1 < K2, !differ(K1, K2), !differ(K2, K1).
twin(K1) :- ky(K1, A), ky(K2, B), K1 > K2, !differ(K1, K2), !differ(K2, K1).
oddk(K) :- ky(K, A), !twin(K).
odd_square(Y, X) :- oddk(K), cid(Y0, X0, K), off(DY, DX), Y = Y0 + DY, X = X0 + DX.

why: red cells cluster per square (gap <= 2); exactly one cluster has a pattern no other cluster has, and its box grown by 1 is the square
invariants: cell colours inside the chosen square

reading: Four yellow cells mark the corners of a rectangle; its strict interior is filled with red (2).

new_rows.name: inside
new_rows.datalog: inside(Y, X) :- cell(Y1, X1, C), cell(Y1, X2, C), cell(Y2, X1, C), cell(Y2, X2, C), Y1 < Y2, X1 < X2, px(Y, X, B), Y > Y1, Y < Y2, X > X1, X < X2.

why: every cell strictly inside a four-corner rectangle becomes 2; corners and everything else unchanged

reading: A small key block (left of the grey separator) shows a lattice of coloured vertical and horizontal lines with set crossings; the output is the marker panel redrawn with that lattice, lines placed at the rows/columns marked by the yellow edge markers.

slots.key: the small line pattern block beside the grey (5) separator/block
slots.canvas: the panel holding the yellow (4) markers; output has its size
slots.vertical_lines: columns marked on the top/bottom edge, coloured in order by the key's vertical lines
slots.horizontal_lines: rows marked on the left/right edge, coloured in order by the key's horizontal lines
slots.crossings: each crossing takes the key's corresponding crossing colour (which line is on top)

why: line counts in the key equal the marked row/column counts; all other output cells are 0

reading: The input splits into a shape half (8 on 0) and a colour half; each coloured cell of the colour half becomes a copy of the shape in that colour (Kronecker product), empty cells become empty blocks.

slots.block(i,j): shape recoloured to colours[i][j], or all 0 if colours[i][j]=0

why: output size = colours size x shape size; every block is the shape in one colour or empty
invariants: shape pattern in every non-empty block

reading: An 8-panel holds a legend of small coloured 3x3 shapes. Each 5x5 red box with a blue pattern becomes a solid box of the legend colour whose shape matches the pattern (up to rotation/reflection); each solid coloured box becomes a red box with that colour's legend shape drawn in blue.

slots.pattern_box: 5x5 box: 2 frame, 1-pattern in the 3x3 interior -> solid box of the colour whose legend shape equals the pattern under rotation/reflection
slots.solid_box: 5x5 box of one colour c -> 2 frame with legend shape of c (same orientation) drawn in 1

why: each box is replaced in place, the legend panel and background never change

reading: Every pair of orthogonally adjacent red cells gets a green (3) outline in the surrounding background cells; single red cells are untouched.

new_rows.name: halo
new_rows.datalog:
adj(Y, X, Y2, X2) :- cell(Y, X, C), Y2 = Y + 1, X2 = X, cell(Y2, X2, D).
adj(Y, X, Y2, X2) :- cell(Y, X, C), Y2 = Y - 1, X2 = X, cell(Y2, X2, D).
adj(Y, X, Y2, X2) :- cell(Y, X, C), Y2 = Y, X2 = X + 1, cell(Y2, X2, D).
adj(Y, X, Y2, X2) :- cell(Y, X, C), Y2 = Y, X2 = X - 1, cell(Y2, X2, D).
deg(Y, X, count(Y2, X2)) :- adj(Y, X, Y2, X2).
pairc(Y, X) :- adj(Y, X, Y2, X2), deg(Y, X, N), N = 1, deg(Y2, X2, M), M = 1.
halo(Y, X) :- pairc(Y0, X0), off(DY, DX), Y = Y0 + DY, X = X0 + DX, px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C).

why: exactly the background cells 8-adjacent to a 2-cell domino become 3

reading: A colour sequence at the top paints each grey diagonal band in nested chevron layers: the band's leading row and edge get the first colour, the next layer the second, and so on, the innermost layer continuing to the band's end.

slots.key: the horizontal run of colours in the top rows
slots.subject: each 5-coloured diagonal band
slots.layer(cell): depth = min(distance from the band's top row, distance from its leading diagonal edge); colour = key[depth], cycling through the key along the band and capped by the band width

why: only 5-cells change; each becomes a key colour determined by its layer depth
